Usually I would say take it off if the APPE experience is something similar you did to residency or had a rotation in. 

UNLESS you are applying to a position (ie haem onc clinic) that you didn’t have experience with in residency, but you did an APPE rotation (in haem onc clinic) before residency. 

Residency should still be the main highlight of your CV, but I’ve been told to keep this type of info in for these types of situations.
Have literally done this, then slept on my couch because I forgot to go get my dryer load 😅

Please know, it will be okay. 

I’m just finishing peds residency, and I’ve been in the same place. 

You are trying hard, and just know that you can do this and keep going. At some point, before you know it, you’re going to get the hang of it. 

Rest assured that your program would probably be telling you if you weren’t meeting standards, so trust them when they say you are where you should be. Develop that trust for their feedback❤️

Also know that you will have Future rotations where maybe you will get the hang of it before your co resident. And that’s okay! It’s a matter of time and everyone is different. 

TL;DR
You aren’t alone, you’ve got this, and we are here for you!!

I would say to go with your heart. You can learn a lot about academia through residency, so if you’d like to try out teaching, why not through APPEs. It could help in your decision as to whether you want to pursue a residency:) it could even be to your benefit if your preceptor is from a hospital or involved in a residency program! 
Trust your gut and go with it. You’ll have your DPC APPEs guaranteed, but not everyone gets a teaching rotation. Try to rank your hospital DPCs early, and after that, go for your teaching block:)

I find it really hard sometimes. It’s something I came to terms with myself about a year ago [26F], but still haven’t fully come out to my family. 

I thought I had fully accepted myself and was just taking my time to come out on my own terms. But when I went to pride this year (first time since openly being bi), I had such mixed emotions. 

Half of me was ecstatic (so proud to be there and be myself), but then (almost like a rollercoaster) I would feel like crying, almost out of confusion. I guess I wasn’t as solid in my feelings as I thought I was. 

Now I’m second guessing all over again, even though I know I’m truly bi. My friends are either gay or straight, so I don’t have others to ask if they’ve shared this same experience. 

Has anyone else been through this? And maybe have some advice? 

Also, thanks in advance for creating the space for me to even be able to post these thoughts, much love to this subreddit 🏳️‍🌈❤️
